structures.label: Thyroid cartilage
structures.description: The largest unpaired laryngeal cartilage; its anterior plates help protect the larynx.

structures.label: Cricoid cartilage
structures.description: An unpaired cartilage inferior to the thyroid cartilage. It forms a complete ring around the airway, with a wider posterior lamina.

structures.label: Left arytenoid cartilage
structures.description: Paired cartilage on the posterior cricoid; its vocal process anchors the posterior end of a vocal ligament.

structures.label: Right arytenoid cartilage
structures.description: Paired cartilage on the posterior cricoid; its vocal process anchors the posterior end of a vocal ligament.

structures.label: Left vocal fold
structures.description: One of the true vocal folds, attached anteriorly near the thyroid cartilage and posteriorly to an arytenoid; its vibration helps produce voice.

candidate_model.note: The official ISA index lists a left vocal ligament, but a vocal ligament is NOT equivalent to the whole true vocal fold; no verified exact fold mesh is mapped.

structures.label: Right vocal fold
structures.description: One of the true vocal folds, attached anteriorly near the thyroid cartilage and posteriorly to an arytenoid; its vibration helps produce voice.

candidate_model.note: The official ISA index lists a right vocal ligament, but a vocal ligament is NOT equivalent to the whole true vocal fold; no verified exact fold mesh is mapped.

structures.label: Left posterior cricoarytenoid
structures.description: The posterior cricoarytenoid is the sole muscle that abducts the true vocal folds, opening the glottis during breathing.

structures.label: Right posterior cricoarytenoid
structures.description: The posterior cricoarytenoid is the sole muscle that abducts the true vocal folds, opening the glottis during breathing.

structures.label: Left lateral cricoarytenoid
structures.description: The lateral cricoarytenoid adducts the true vocal folds through medial arytenoid rotation, helping close the glottis.

structures.label: Right lateral cricoarytenoid
structures.description: The lateral cricoarytenoid adducts the true vocal folds through medial arytenoid rotation, helping close the glottis.

review_prompts.question: Which is the largest cartilage of the larynx?
review_prompts.explanation: The thyroid cartilage is the largest laryngeal cartilage; the drawing does not reproduce its anatomy.

review_prompts.question: Which laryngeal cartilage forms a complete ring around the airway?
review_prompts.explanation: Cricoid is a complete cartilaginous ring inferior to thyroid; the schematic torus is not a verified shape.

review_prompts.question: Which paired cartilage provides the vocal process where a vocal ligament attaches posteriorly?
review_prompts.explanation: Arytenoid vocal processes provide the posterior ligament attachment. Their depicted location remains approximate.

review_prompts.question: Which paired structures vibrate to help produce voiced sound?
review_prompts.explanation: The true vocal folds provide a vibratory sound source during voiced phonation; the static shapes do not simulate vibration.

review_prompts.question: Which intrinsic laryngeal muscle is the sole abductor of the true vocal folds?
review_prompts.explanation: Posterior cricoarytenoid abducts the vocal folds, opening the glottis. No valid motion is simulated.

review_prompts.question: Which cricoarytenoid muscle adducts the true vocal folds?
review_prompts.explanation: Lateral cricoarytenoid adducts the folds by rotating arytenoid cartilage; the picture does not show that real muscle path.

review_prompts.question: Which cartilage provides the joint surface beneath the paired arytenoid cartilages?
review_prompts.answer: The posterior part of the cricoid cartilage.
review_prompts.explanation: Each arytenoid articulates with the superior/posterior cricoid region. Their precise positions are not represented here.

review_prompts.question: Where do the true vocal folds attach at the front and back of the larynx?
review_prompts.answer: Anteriorly at the thyroid cartilage and posteriorly at the arytenoid cartilages.
review_prompts.explanation: These paired attachment relationships matter for phonation; the schematic rods cannot be used to measure them.

review_prompts.question: Which folds are the primary vibratory source in normal voiced speech: true vocal folds or vestibular (false) folds?
review_prompts.explanation: The vestibular folds are a different pair and are intentionally not modeled in this scene.

review_prompts.question: How do the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles act differently on the true vocal folds?
review_prompts.answer: Posterior cricoarytenoid abducts them; lateral cricoarytenoid adducts them.
review_prompts.explanation: Abduction increases the glottal opening, while adduction brings the folds closer. No mechanical animation is validated.

review_prompts.question: Which intrinsic laryngeal muscle is the main exception to recurrent laryngeal nerve motor innervation?
review_prompts.explanation: Its motor supply usually comes from the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve; the cricothyroid is not shown in this viewer.

review_prompts.question: Which nerve generally provides motor innervation to the intrinsic laryngeal muscles other than cricothyroid?
review_prompts.answer: The recurrent laryngeal nerve, via its inferior laryngeal branch.
review_prompts.explanation: This is an anatomy-learning statement, not a test of nerve injury or diagnosis; the nerves are not modeled.

coverage.included_meshes: Ten original schematic placeholders. Not anatomically validated.
omitted_structures: Vocal ligament layers and detailed glottal geometry
coverage.statement: The scene is an intentionally incomplete larynx illustration; omitted structures are NOT absent from human anatomy.

learning_objectives.label: Distinguish major laryngeal cartilages
learning_objectives.statement: Identify the thyroid, cricoid and paired arytenoid cartilages and explain one key anatomical relationship for each.

learning_objectives.label: Explain true vocal-fold function
learning_objectives.statement: Identify the true vocal folds, their main attachment sites, and their role in phonation; distinguish them from unmodeled vestibular folds.

learning_objectives.label: Compare intrinsic laryngeal muscle actions
learning_objectives.statement: Contrast posterior cricoarytenoid abduction with lateral cricoarytenoid adduction, and connect those actions to changes in the glottal opening.

learning_objectives.label: Describe principal motor innervation
learning_objectives.statement: State the usual recurrent-laryngeal-nerve motor supply of intrinsic laryngeal muscles and its cricothyroid exception.
